title: Flexbox Best Practices and Exercises knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Flexbox Best Practices and Exercises”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Choosing Flexbox for one-dimensional layouts” under “Flexbox Best Practices and Exercises”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with flexbox best practices and exercises?
options: Use the main and cross axes deliberately, with a gap and wrapping when content can grow.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Use the main and cross axes deliberately, with a gap and wrapping when content can grow.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Use the main and cross axes deliberately, with a gap and wrapping when content can grow. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Flexbox Best Practices and Exercises” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
